rows.stated:
SIDE-rcurve · Criterion.lean
  ============================

  The R-Curve EQUIVALENCE engine — checkpoint 1.2-D.

  Verifies the structural/logical core of the PROVEN Equivalence
  Chain (R_CURVE_CRITERION_v0_1, consolidating P22 Phases 1–66):
  RH ⟺ V strictly monotone on every R-curve in {σ > 1/2}.

  CLOSURE: the positivity Re(ξ′/ξ) > 0 driving the monotonicity is
  CLOSED via the Phase-66 SIDE closure (off-line zeros excluded from
  the seven-class catalogue, sealed by Conservation), not an open
  margin. The route shares its bottom step with the deposited proof
  (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.19938917); this kernel verifies the
  equivalence machinery. Conclusive checkpoint, not a flagged reach.

  Source: R_CURVE_CRITERION_v0_1; P22_PHASE66_SIDE_CLOSURE;
  P22_RCURVE_MONOTONICITY_REVISED.
rows.licensed: The file compiles only elementary real lemmas (a strictly monotone V vanishes at most once, a field identity, Re((a+bi)/(Vi)) = b/V, n/b > 0, a defined codim count); no declaration mentions xi, RH or an R-curve, and "CLOSED via the Phase-66 SIDE closure (off-line zeros excluded from the seven-class catalogue, sealed by Conservation)" states the open clause (catalogue exhaustiveness and Conservation) as closed.
rows.action: RE-CUT: Compiles elementary lemmas used by the R-curve criterion -- a strictly monotone real function vanishes at most once, alpha^2/beta + beta = (alpha^2 + beta^2)/beta, Re((alpha + beta i)/(V i)) = beta/V, n/beta > 0 for positive n and beta, and a defined codimension count; neither RH <-> monotonicity nor Re(xi'/xi) > 0 is stated here, and the SIDE closure it rests on (catalogue exhaustiveness, Conservation) is the open clause.

rows.stated:
## T1 — the engine: strict monotonicity ⟹ at most one zero

This is the decisive (ii)⟹(i) step. A strictly monotone V is
injective, so it vanishes at most once.
rows.licensed: monotone_unique_zero is only "a strictly monotone V is injective, so it vanishes at most once"; the (ii) => (i) step from monotonicity to RH also needs an off-line zero to force a second vanishing of V, which no declaration states, so "This is the decisive (ii) => (i) step" claims more.
rows.action: RE-CUT: The elementary half of the (ii) => (i) step: a strictly monotone V is injective, so it vanishes at most once.

rows.stated: ## T2 — the Monotonicity Formula shape  V′ = |ξ′|²/β
rows.licensed: monotonicity_formula compiles alpha^2/beta + beta = (alpha^2 + beta^2)/beta, which the section names as the formula's shape.

rows.stated: ## T3 — the Beta–V identity  Re(ξ′/ξ) = β/V on the curve (ξ = iV)
rows.licensed: beta_V_re compiles Re((alpha + beta i)/(V i)) = beta/V, the identity under xi' = alpha + i beta and xi = iV.

rows.stated: ## T4 — Singular Repulsion: positive numerator over positive β gives V′ > 0
rows.licensed: singular_repulsion is 0 < n and 0 < beta -> 0 < n/beta.

rows.stated:
## T5 — codimension of the zero condition

On-line zero: V = 0 (codim 1). Off-line zero: V = 0 ∧ β = 0
simultaneously (codim 2).
rows.licensed: zero_codim is defined as 1 on-line and 2 off-line, with rfl checks; the V = 0 and beta = 0 reading is the model the definition encodes.
second_zero_breaks_monotone: strict monotonicity and two distinct zeros give False; that an off-line zero "would force" a second zero is stated as the argument, not as compiled.
